newsitem.title: USA: Earlier U.S. equity options close aims to cut risk.
newsitem.headline: Earlier U.S. equity options close aims to cut risk.

text.p: Market makers in Hewlett-Packard Co options were left holding the bag for five minutes on Thursday after the company reported disappointing earnings.
The company's fiscal second quarter earnings were released at about 1605 EDT/2005 GMT, five minutes after the underlying shares stopped trading but five minutes before the options closed.
For those five minutes, the options market became the primary marketplace -- sharply increasing the risk for those who sell the options.
But come June 23, such risk will be minimized when U.S. options exchanges advance the close of equity and narrow-based index options trading by eight minutes to 1602 EDT/2002 GMT.
On Thursday, three of the four U.S. options exchanges won Securities and Exchange Commission approval to move those closes up.
"I'm happy -- it's over," Michael Schwartz, head of the industry's Committee on Options, said on Friday. Schwartz had pushed to get the exchanges together on the issue.

The American Stock Exchange, Chicago Board Options Exchange and Pacific Stock Exchange were approved for the earlier close, and a Philadelpia Stock Exchange plan to do the same is linked to a proposal that is out for public comment.
A spokeswoman for the Philadelphia exchange said it expects to begin the earlier closes on June 23 as well.

"The 4:02 closing time will go a long way toward eliminating market disruptions when news announcements, particularly earnings reports, are made when the cash market is closed but the options market is still open," CBOE President Charles Henry said in a statement.
Options industry players said the change was long overdue and should prevent customers from getting overpriced options after the underlying market closes.

"Market makers become the primary market after 4 o'clock," Schwartz, a managing director at Oppenheimer & Co, said. "With all the news items coming out in this period of time, their liability is increased many-fold."

Options traders say options close later than stocks because market makers and specialists need to see final closing prices of the shares before they can close the options. This process typically takes a couple of minutes after share trading ends.
Matthew Zahner, a market maker at the Pacific Exchange, said the earlier closes will improve the climate for customers.

"When we take extra risk, we have to factor in that risk because we can't hedge," he said. "So customers may not get the fills they think they would get if the market were open and we could hedge things."
He said that while options can be priced off so-called third market trading, or off-exchange trading, liquidity is typically too thin to price them appropriately.
Some exchanges have asked companies scheduled to report earnings after the stock market close to wait until after the options close to release the news.

"A lot of companies release earnings after the stock close not realizing the options are still open," said John Streibich, a market maker in Hewlett options at the CBOE. "It creates a lot of problems. The earlier close will relieve us of that problem."
